       Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hodge
         on behalf of Himself and His Family


                                                         Bradford W. Bayliff
                                                    State Bar No. 24012260
                                                             (512) 225-0027
                                                          Brad@Bayliff.Law

                                              Bayliff Law Firm PLLC
                                                     420 Crosswind Drive
                                                      Blanco, Texas 78606

                                                           Attorney for
                                               Ryan and Stacy Hodge

                                                              May 22, 2026




                             1 of 5
 Q.   Please introduce yourself and identify on whose behalf you are testifying.
A.   My name is Ryan Hodge. My family and I live at 3661 Thomas Arnold Road. I am
     a lifelong resident of Salado, Texas. I am the fifth generation of my family in this
     community and my children are the sixth.

Q.   Are you the same Ryan Hodge who filed direct testimony in this proceeding?
A.   Yes. I filed Direct Testimony on behalf of myself and my family.

Q.   What is the purpose of your cross-rebuttal testimony?
A.   The purpose of my cross-rebuttal testimony is to respond to assertions made by another
     witness in this proceeding.

Q.   To what witness are you responding?
A.   I am responding to Mike Michaux. He filed direct testimony on his and Lisa Michaux’s
     behalf, Solana Development Corporation, and Solana Development, L.P.

Q.   Do you know Mike and Lisa Michaux?
A.   Yes. My family has been in the Salado area for almost 100 years. I am the fifth generation
     of my family to raise my family in Salado. Our families have known each other for
     decades.

Q.   Why are you responding to him in cross-rebuttal testimony?
A.   The Michaux property is not the only high-quality, environmentally sensitive land in our
     area. The alternative route Mr. Michaux’s expert recommends – Route 392 – shifts the
     same impacts onto other long-stewarded properties and crosses Salado Creek three times
     instead of once, two other springs, Mustang Creek and Watkins Creek. Avoiding Solana
     Ranch will cause harm to others.




                          Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hodge
                                             2
 Stewardship, conservation, and environmental significance

Q.     Mr. Michaux filed testimony on the stewardship, conservation, and environmental
       significance of Solana Ranch. What is your response?
A.     Mr. Michaux described spring-fed water flowing through Solana Ranch, including Salado
       Creek, Rumsey Creek, and Buttermilk Creek. Spring-fed waters are throughout our area.
       Salado Creek’s springs influenced early settlement decisions in our historic town and
       continue to be important to all of us in Salado.
              Our property includes extensive frontage along spring-fed waters of Salado Creek
       and Watkins Branch, a tributary of Salado Creek, with clear, spring‑fed, rock‑bottom
       waters, mature live oak stands, and limestone bluffs rising up to approximately seventy
       feet. The Watkins Branch headwaters are the Elm Springs, which Route 392 also goes
       over and it crosses Mustang Creek just below Willingham Springs. Like on Solana Ranch,
       these features support wildlife habitat and reflect the natural character of the Hill Country
       landscape that defines this area.

Q.     Mr. Michaux describes Salado Creek as an environmentally sensitive feature of
       Solana Ranch. What is your response?
A.     I understand his concern. My father, my aunt, and I expressed similar concerns in our
       direct testimonies. My review of the maps from the application show that Route 894 will
       cross Salado Creek once on the Solana Ranch. Mr. Michaux’s expert witness
       recommends Route 392, which will cross the same Salado Creek that Mr. Michaux says is
       environmentally sensitive, except it will cross the Creek three times instead of once and it
       also crosses Watkins Creek and Mustang Creek.

Q.     Mr. Michaux discussed recognition his family has received for its stewardship
       efforts. What is your response?
A.     They have been good stewards of the land, but so have we and others in our community.
       From years of being active in real estate in the community, I know there are numerous
       landowners who follow great stewardship practices.




                           Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hodge
                                              3
 Long-term family ownership

Q.    Is Solana Ranch’s long-term family ownership unique in the area?
A.    The properties in our area around Salado have many examples of long-term family
      ownership and stewardship of the land. Links E7, E11, and E12, are part of Route 392. Mr.
      Michaux’s expert recommends go through our family’s land, the Cornett family’s Tenroc
      Ranch, Monteith Ranch, Smith Ranch, Davine Springs Ranch, and Summers Mill Ranch
      on Salado Creek. All of these ranches have been good stewards of the land.
             Arthur MacArthur Monteith of Belton established the Monteith Ranch, with its
      iconic Bar-V-Bar brand and a legacy built on stewardship and resilience. The Monteith
      Ranch has been in continuous operation for over 117 years.

Development of the Solana Ranch and E7 and E12 area

Q.    Mr. Michaux discusses development of the Solana Ranch. How do you respond?
A.    My family is active in the real estate business in our community. We know and
      understand development is taking place in our community. Mr. Michaux acknowledges in
      his testimony that it becomes very difficult to keep family interests aligned while
      preserving a property like Solana Ranch. I understand their decision and hope it works out
      well for them and the community.
             Mr. Michaux describes a partnership with a developer he says has had success in
      executing large-scale projects across the country. He describes a future Solana Ranch
      community of up to 14,000 houses, along with schools, parks, and retail offices.
      Unfortunately, it sounds to me the future of Solana Ranch Mr. Michaux describes will be
      a property filled with mass development including immense amount of construction and
      building to handle the 14,000 future homes.

Q.    Is Solana Ranch an active development at this time?
A.    No. It is my understanding it is in the planning stage. No homes have been built and no
      infrastructure constructed.




                          Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hodge
                                             4
 Q.    Will Route 392, the route Solana Ranch affect you and others?
A.    I understand the prospect of a transmission line affecting their long-term plans is
      something they object to. Route 392, the route Solana Ranch recommends to avoid its
      property, will affect Salado Creek, our family’s homes, the Salado ISD, Salado’s
      immediate growth due to the proximity to the Village of Salado, numerous other
      developers’ projects, and numerous existing residential homes. The Salado ISD filed
      testimony objecting to the construction of the transmission line near our community
      school complex. The Stagecoach Inn filed testimony expressing concern about proximity
      of Link E12 to Salado’s historic downtown and effects on tourism. Many intervenor
      homeowners filed direct testimony expressing their concerns about proximity to the
      school.

Conclusion

Q.    Please summarize your overall position on the transmission line routing, the key
      impacts on your property, and specific actions you are asking the Commission to
      take.
A.    Routing options that do not use E12, E11, and E7 would substantially reduce impacts to
      our family, neighboring residences, Salado Creek, and the historic core of the community,
      while still allowing the project to meet its purpose. We therefore ask the Commission to
      approve a route that avoids Links E12 and E7 and minimizes permanent impacts to
      homes, children, and established community resources.

Q.    Confirm that your testimony and exhibits are true and correct, were prepared by you
      or under your direction, that you expect to be available for cross-examination, and
      that you stipulate other parties may treat your testimony as if filed under oath.
A.    Yes, I confirm all this.




                           Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hodge
